content.title: Put appointment details where you’ll find them
content.summary: A little admin now can spare you a search later. Keep a nonurgent appointment contact easy to reach.
steps: Open the official website of a clinic you use or would consider for a future nonurgent appointment.
Find its appointment phone number or booking page, opening hours, and any new-patient or payment information you need.
Save those details in your usual contacts or note; mark anything you still need to confirm with the clinic.
content.done_when: One clinic’s appointment contact and any unanswered practical questions are saved.

content.title: Leave your pet’s routine ready to share
content.summary: Make it easier for a future helper to follow the ordinary routine your pet already knows.
steps: Write your pet’s usual food, feeding times, water routine and everyday needs without changing their existing care.
Note where the everyday supplies are and add your usual vet’s contact details.
Save the note privately where you can share it with an agreed helper; leave keys, codes and home-entry details out.
content.done_when: A private everyday-care note is ready to share with a helper you choose.

eligible_resources.name: Rover — pet sitter research
eligible_resources.purpose: Compare potential paid drop-in sitters for cats or dogs in your area before you need one.
eligible_resources.limits: Research is free; bookings cost money. Coverage, prices, pet types, experience and dates vary. A listing is not a confirmed booking or guarantee of suitability.

eligible_resources.name: Pet Sitters International — sitter finder
eligible_resources.purpose: Find member pet-care businesses to contact about future drop-in care, experience with the pet, notice and an introductory meeting.
eligible_resources.limits: PSI does not inspect or endorse listed businesses. Ask the provider about fees, visit notice, meeting first, and what happens if they cannot attend. A lead or inquiry is not agreed care.
